prompt:
Model a lead-screw linear actuator as the three parts `frame`, `screw` and `carriage`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The frame is a 60 mm square plate, 8 mm thick, centred on the origin (z = -4 to +4), with a 10 mm diameter screw bore straight through it on the Z axis. The screw is a plain 9.8 mm diameter pilot cylinder, 30 mm long, standing in that bore with its lower end flush with the plate underside - 0.1 mm radial air all round. The carriage is a 12 mm square block, 6 mm tall, riding beside the screw with its centre on the X axis at x = 18, floating 0.5 mm above the plate top.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: the frame's bore wall as `screw_bore` and its top face as `travel_face`; the screw's cylindrical surface as `screw_pilot`; the carriage's underside as `guide_foot` and its top face as `nose`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-motor` (parent `frame:screw_bore`, child `screw:screw_pilot`, travel 0 to 3600 degrees - ten turns), a prismatic joint `j-carriage` (parent `frame:travel_face`, child `carriage:guide_foot`, travel 0 to 24 mm), and the coupling `cp-leadscrew` driving the carriage from the motor at the metric lead of 2 mm per revolution (ratio 2/360 mm per degree, offset 0). The carriage is then a dependent parameter - poses and sweeps assign only the motor. Evaluate the declared mechanism with check_motion once it is in place.

Build all three parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

entry.note: the screw pilot runs on the bore axis: one nut line, no wobble
ten turns of motor travel end to end (KINEMATICS.md §1)
carriage travel window: the 20 mm working stroke plus overtravel margin to the hard stop

sweeping only the FREE motor parameter, the coupling must carry the nose to the top-of-stroke handoff point (zero nose at z 10.5 + 20 mm stroke): a run that never declares cp-leadscrew leaves the carriage parked at zero and misses by the whole stroke
the carriage never runs into the frame anywhere over the stroke
